newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN STATE NOTES ISSUE RAISES 8.65 BLN BFR.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN STATE NOTES ISSUE RAISES 8.65 BLN BFR.

text.p: The Belgian finance ministry said on Tuesday that the fourth issue of two types of state notes had raised a total 8.65 billion Belgian francs by the end of the subscription period.
The ministry said in a statement that in the latest issue it had altogether sold 5.925 billion francs of five-year notes, extendable to seven years. The notes carry a fixed coupon of 4.50 percent.
Notes with revisable coupons and put options after three, five and seven years raised 2.725 billion francs.
The issue was the latest in a new series of treasury products targeted at retail investors and designed to help Belgium meet its borrowing requirements.
It brought the total raised from the first four issues to 53.25 billion Belgian francs, well below the 85 billion franc target believed set by the finance ministry and treasury.
The failure to place all the planned paper could leave the commercial banks that agreed to market and manage the state notes programme open to fines.
A finance ministry official said, however, he believed no fines would be levied.
A spokesman for the treasury, which is responsible for the project's management and the agreement with the banks, was not immediately available to comment.
